items.followUp: What happens to DNA during the S phase of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: During S phase, DNA is synthesised or replicated.
rubric.description: Identifies DNA synthesis or replication as the key event of S phase
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is replicated or synthesised during S phase.

rubric.why: DNA replication duplicates each chromosome, producing two sister chromatids.
rubric.description: States the result of DNA replication
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromosomes are duplicated or that a duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids.

modelAnswer: S phase is the synthesis phase of interphase, during which DNA is replicated.
As a result, each chromosome is duplicated and consists of two sister chromatids.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of enzymes and give one example of an enzyme.

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions without being used up.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzymes as biological catalysts or stating that they speed up reactions without being consumed.

rubric.why: Enzymes are specific to particular substrates or reactions.
rubric.description: Gives a second distinct characteristic of enzymes
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.

items.followUp: How does dietary fibre help prevent constipation?

rubric.why: Dietary fibre adds bulk to intestinal contents and faeces.
rubric.description: States that dietary fibre adds bulk
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fibre adds bulk to faeces, stool, or intestinal contents.

rubric.why: Fibre helps contents move through the digestive tract and makes bowel movements easier, helping prevent constipation.
rubric.description: States the benefit of fibre for bowel movement
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking fibre with easier passage of faeces, easier bowel movements, or prevention of constipation.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibres, also called roughage, add bulk to the contents of the intestine and to faeces.
They help food and faeces move through the digestive tract and make bowel movements easier, helping to prevent constipation.
